title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed an artifact-backed paired experiment that measures whether inserting a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) into a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated configuration proposals while satisfying a latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired operator intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed: baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975), guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The run used a preregistered shared-initial-candidate design (observed model_calls_used = 401 vs preregistered planned_model_calls = 800); full per-episode artifacts, validator traces, provider-call logs, and execution manifest are archived. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) cannot be evaluated because end‑to‑end latency telemetry was not archived; this missingness is disclosed and discussed. All principal numbers reported here are reproduced from archived artifacts (paths and SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest).

sections.introduction:
Automating translation from operator intent to device configuration promises major operational efficiency gains, but LLM-generated proposals can be unsafe in production without rigorous validation. The conventional mitigation is a generate–validate–repair pipeline: an LLM proposes configuration, an automated verifier (digital twin or formal checker) assesses functional correctness, and repair or human escalation follows when validation fails. Full verification of every proposal can be latency-expensive and impractical for low-latency workflows. We evaluate a selective, low-latency verification intervention: risk-score generated candidates and run a fast verifier only on high‑risk proposals (the “guarded” condition) vs accepting LLM output without selective verification (the “baseline”).
Research question (preregistered, CAND-2026-001): Can a selective low-latency verification tier integrated into a generate–validate–repair pipeline reduce unsafe commits versus LLM-only while meeting a preregistered latency SLO? Our preregistered confirmatory hypotheses: H1 (safety) — guarded < baseline unsafe-commit rate (paired); H2 (latency) — guarded meets 95th‑percentile ≤ 2000 ms and is statistically lower than the full-checker baseline while improving safety over LLM-only. We executed the preregistered plan autonomously and archived all raw and processed artifacts; key artifact paths and SHA‑256 identifiers are recorded in the execution manifest and in the mandatory Disclosure Statement below.
sections.related_work: Recent work has evaluated LLM-driven configuration generation, verifier‑guided repair, and agentic NetOps with digital twins. Representative artifact-backed nearest work includes: Cornetto-style configuration-repair benchmarks that couple synthesis and formal verification (arXiv:2604.22513), agentic verifier-augmented evaluation reporting agentic architectures and verifier loops (arXiv:2606.06212), and agentic NetOps integrating digital twins for validation (arXiv:2604.18233). Formal verification and header-space/NetKAT approaches supply the theory for functional checks (e.g., functional network-modeling literature including RouteNet-Fermi for performance modeling [IEEE/COMNET artifacts]). Our study differs by preregistering a paired confirmatory design, executing end-to-end with deterministic validators, and publishing full per-episode provenance enabling deterministic reproduction of all reported counts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan
- Preregistration ID: CAND-2026-001 (frozen prior to execution). The preregistered plan defines tasks (400 paired intents), model(s) (declared generator: gpt-5-mini), conditions (baseline, guarded), primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), retry and missingness rules, and power assumptions (target 5 percentage-point absolute reduction with N=400). The preregistration artifact and SHA are archived; see Disclosure Statement for the immutable master-prompt reference.
Corpus and task generation
- A deterministic synthetic task generator produced 400 operator intents spanning interface edits, routing changes, and ACL-like edits. Ten percent (40/400) are deterministic adversarial/OOD variants per the preregistered perturbation rules. Each task manifest includes initial and expected-final states, intent text, and required safe-change patterns. Representative task manifests and reference answers are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Example: pair-000001 manifest and per-condition artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, SHA-256: ea8359dbe5a5d054278e24f3...).
Models, pipeline, and design choices
- Model: gpt-5-mini (declared in execution/model_configuration.json; artifact SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da...). Pipeline modes: baseline (LLM-only acceptance) and guarded (risk scorers + fast verifier, then deterministic full-checker for final scoring). The run used a preregistered shared-initial-candidate design (independent_condition_generation=false) to isolate verifier/repair effects given the same generated candidate; this was allowed in the preregistration and materially reduced model calls in execution (see reconciliation below).
Scoring and deterministic validator
- Ground truth scorer/validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator id and version archived). The scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation: a proposal is scored valid only if the deterministic validator confirms the candidate meets the intent-specified constraints and network rules. Per-episode scorer JSONs record normalized configurations, parsed command counts, validator verdicts, and the detailed validator trace (execution/scoring/*.json). Example per-episode scorer JSON artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA-256: ea8359dbe5...).
Statistical analysis (preregistered)
- Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided on paired binary outcomes. Confidence interval: paired bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Missingness and retry policy followed the preregistered rules; infrastructure failures cause pair exclusion from the primary analysis (none occurred). All analysis artifacts and logs are archived (analysis/*; hashes provided).
sections.results:
Execution and deterministic reconciliation
- Planned_model_calls in the preregistration enumerated 800 (400 intents × 2 conditions × 1 generation under independent-generation accounting). The executed shared-initial design produced model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair); this is reconciled and documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and the execution manifest (provider-call audit shows stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 400, "repair": 1}). All provider-call logs are archived under execution/provider_calls/ with SHA‑256 entries.
Confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed)
- Complete pairs: 400 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; SHA-256: 9266951e...).
- Baseline valid proposals: 399/400 = 0.9975 (analysis/condition_summary.csv; SHA-256: 0d6efc16...).
- Guarded valid proposals: 400/400 = 1.000.
- Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256: a6906bb4...).
- Primary estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Analysis logs and bootstrap parameters are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; SHA-256: 9ea0d56d...).
Representative diagnostic: discordant episode
- The single discordant pair (n10=1) is archived and inspectable. See execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (baseline failed; SHA-256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (guarded valid; SHA-256: d0cbfe9a...). The per-episode validator traces show a dependency violation in the baseline candidate that the guarded pipeline corrected prior to final validation; those scorer JSONs and validator traces provide the exact sequence and can be replayed from the provider-call logs.
Latency SLO (H2) status
- H2 required artifact-backed timing telemetry for the end-to-end pipeline (generation, risk scoring, fast verifier, full-checker) to compute 95th-percentile latency. The confirmatory artifact bundle does not include these per-stage timestamps or end‑to‑end latency telemetry; this missingness was recorded in execution logs and prevents evaluation of H2. We therefore report H2 as unresolved rather than claiming compliance.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and statistical context
- The baseline success rate (399/400) is near ceiling. With such a high baseline, detecting small absolute gains requires much larger sample sizes or tasks where baseline reliability is lower. The observed paired difference is 0.0025 with a bootstrap 95% CI upper bound 0.0075; this demonstrates the intervention produced at most a small absolute gain under the chosen corpus, model, and deterministic validator. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 reflects the discordance pattern (only one discordant pair) and the ceiling effect; it does not imply the intervention is harmful.
Operational implications
- When LLM generation reliability is already very high under the applied checker, the marginal operational return from selective verification is small. In higher-risk regimes (lower baseline reliability, adversarial pools, or production heterogeneity), selective verification budgets and fast verifiers may yield larger, operationally meaningful safety improvements. We recommend follow-up runs targeted at lower-baseline tasks and increased adversarial coverage to map the verification-budget vs unsafe-commit Pareto frontier.
Design trade-offs: shared-initial vs independent-generation
- The preregistered shared-initial-candidate design (executed here) reduces generator-induced variance and isolates the verifier/repair effect given the same generated proposal, which is a well-defined estimand for contexts that cache or deterministically reuse a candidate across downstream checks. It does, however, alter the estimand from an independent-generation design in which each condition would receive an independently sampled generator output. We document this design choice and reconcile planned_model_calls vs observed model_calls (planned 800 vs observed 401) deterministically in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. Both designs are operationally relevant; selection should match the real-world orchestration being evaluated.
Failure-mode evidence and reproducibility
- All per-episode validator traces, scorer JSONs, provider-call logs, and raw responses are archived and SHA‑256 cataloged. Inspecting discordant episodes (e.g., pair-000149) allows precise diagnosis of how the guarded pipeline mitigated a dependency violation. Example artifact paths and SHA‑256: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (ea8359dbe5a5d054278e24f3...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (431f61c02fac...), and the execution/model_configuration.json (a40e96e2...).
Missing preregistered telemetry and recommended follow-ups
- The absent latency telemetry prevents the preregistered latency analysis (H2). Future runs must record per-stage timestamps (generation, risk scoring, fast verifier, repair, full-checker) and archive them with deterministic hashes. Additional recommendations that are artifact-grounded: (1) repeat under independent-generation to estimate joint generator+verifier effects; (2) expand adversarial/OOD fraction and task diversity to increase power where baseline is high; (3) evaluate multiple generator models and multiple validators to estimate external validity; (4) preregister and record latency traces to test H2.
Threats to validity (artifact-backed)
- Internal validity: shared-initial design changes estimand; archived provider-call logs and reconciliation artifact document observed model-call accounting and confirm adherence to preregistered retry/missingness rules.
- Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 is a digital-twin style checker; real-device divergences may exist (validator traces archive precise checks to aid external validation).
- External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic corpus limit generalizability; these constraints and full artifact list are disclosed.
- Conclusion validity: ceiling effect reduced power to detect small gains; we preregistered power calculations but note the realized baseline was higher than many planning scenarios, a fact documented in artifact-backed condition_summary.csv.
sections.conclusion: This preregistered, artifact-backed paired study found a numerically small safety gain from a selective low-latency verification tier when evaluated on a 400-item synthetic NetOps corpus with gpt-5-mini and a deterministic full-checker; the baseline was near ceiling (399/400), guarded = 400/400, paired difference 0.0025 (95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075]). All reported quantities are reproducible from archived artifacts (responses, scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution manifest). The preregistered latency SLO (H2) could not be evaluated because required latency telemetry was not recorded; we disclose that absence and provide full provenance to enable reproducible follow-ups that record timing and broaden model/validator conditions. Operational deployment decisions should weigh baseline generator reliability, adversarial risk, and verification budget; our archived artifacts permit detailed failure-mode analysis and precise replication of the run.

All model calls, provider logs, and timestamps for provider events are archived under execution/provider_calls/; execution manifest catalogs SHA‑256 for each provider-call artifact.
- Preregistration and design: Study preregistration CAND-2026-001 (frozen prior to execution) defined hypotheses H1/H2, paired confirmatory design, sampling plan (400 paired intents, 10% adversarial/OOD), primary estimand, retry/missingness policy, and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration artifact and its SHA are archived with the evidence bundle.
- Autonomous boundary: Pre-lock humans selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps), developed reusable infrastructure, and approved the master prompt and constraints. After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, artifact archiving, statistical analysis, manuscript drafting, AI-based peer review, and autonomous revision. No manual human editing of technical sections or results occurred post-lock; all final technical text and analyses derive from the autonomous run and archived artifacts.
- Artifacts and reproducibility: All raw outputs (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), validator traces (embedded in scorer JSONs), provider-call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifests (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json), and analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) are archived with SHA‑256 hashes listed in the execution manifest. Representative artifact SHA‑256 entries referenced in the manuscript include: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (ea8359dbe5a5d054278e24f3...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (431f61c02facc2e51e02413e...), and the single discordant pair artifacts execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (d0cbfe9a...). analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256s a6906bb4..., 0d6efc16...) reproduce the principal counts.
- Deviations and missingness: The preregistered plan enumerated planned_model_calls = 800 under an independent-generation accounting convention. The executed shared-initial-candidate design (permitted by the preregistration) produced model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair); this deterministic reconciliation is archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Critically, the preregistered H2 required artifact-backed end-to-end latency telemetry (per-stage timestamps and pipeline latencies); those timing traces were not archived for the confirmatory run. As a result, H2 (latency SLO compliance) is unresolved in this paper and explicitly disclosed. No other post-preregistration analytic changes were made.
- Human oversight: humans performed pre-lock infrastructure development, topic selection, and master-prompt approval. After the autonomy lock, the autonomous system executed all experimental design, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, and revision steps; authorship and accountability are claimed by the Research Director per the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track rules. All execution and artifact hashes are archived to enable independent verification of claims.
- Access note: the full execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) catalogs all archived artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes required to reproduce the reported analyses deterministically.
limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: deterministic task generator, while reproducible, may not capture full linguistic/operational diversity of production intents.
Single-model scope: only gpt-5-mini was used as the generator; external validity across LLM families is unresolved.
Single deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital-twin style) may not capture all real-device semantics; real-device divergences remain possible.
Shared-initial design: the executed shared-initial-candidate design changes the estimand relative to independent-generation; reported effect is conditional on the same generated candidate.
Ceiling effect: baseline success = 399/400 limited statistical power to detect small improvements; larger or lower-baseline cohorts are required to detect modest absolute gains.
Missing preregistered telemetry: per-stage and end-to-end latency traces required for H2 were not archived; H2 is therefore unresolved in this run.
